newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent off in thin trade as market monitors OPEC.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent off in thin trade as market monitors OPEC.

text.p: IPE oil futures eased slightly in quiet trade on Wednesday as the market digested a raft of oil supply-related news and awaited headlines out of the OPEC meeting in Vienna, traders said.

August Brent was trading four cents lower at $17.83 at 1116 GMT having fallen as low as $17.73 a barrel on Tuesday on news that Iraq expected to resume oil exports under the oil-for-food deal in the next seven to ten days.
Gas oil was trading 25 cents lower at $160 a tonne.

The outcome of the OPEC meeting in Vienna was the main focus for the market even though few players were expecting OPEC oil ministers to change the existing oil production ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.
Traders said American Petroleum Institute (API) data released late on Tuesday had been mainly neutral although some of the oil product stock data was regarded as mildly bullish.
According to the API data, crude oil stocks held in primary storage fell 756,000 barrels in the week ended June 20, while gasoline rose 592,000 barrels and middle distillates rose 905,000 barrels.

"The products builds themselves are nothing to write home about, but the fact that gasoline inventories actually rose at this time of year is not what the bulls were hoping for," said Leslie Nicholas at commodity brokers GNI in his daily report.

The prospect of Iraqi exports lurked in the background although traders pointed out that Iraqi oil would not start flowing into international markets again until the aid distribution plan included in the oil-for-food deal had been finalised.

"The distribution plan still has to be agreed between Baghdad and the UN, but the regime does not foresee any problems in the talks, according to officials. However, this could be a tactical play by Iraq and we are by no means convinced about the timetable until evidence of progress is received," said GNI's Nicholas.-- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
